html: Asthma makes the airways extra sensitive. When something sets them off, they tighten and fill with mucus, which can cause wheezing, coughing and a tight chest. With the right plan, most people stay active and in control.

image.alt: Illustration of a pair of lungs
image.caption: A written plan tells you what to do each day and when symptoms flare.
image.title: Illustration of a pair of lungs

html:
• Colds and flu
  • Pollen, mold, animal dander and dust mites
  • Cigarette smoke and smoggy air
  • Cold air or hard exercise

• Make a written asthma action plan with your care team
  • Learn how and when to use each inhaler
  • Keep your rescue inhaler with you
Your rescue inhaler isn't helping, it's hard to speak in full sentences, or your lips or fingernails look gray or blue.
